newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks tumble again to end one pct lower.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks tumble again to end one pct lower.

text.p: Toronto stocks tumbled further on Thursday, extending their recent heavy losses as investors took more profits from Canada's biggest equity market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 58.85 points to close at 5722.84 in brisk turnover of 94.3 million shares worth C$1.62 billion.
Declining issues outnumbered advancers 586 to 386, with 296 issues unchanged.
Analysts said today's session was calmer than Wednesday's selloff when the key index sank 138 points or 2.3 percent for its sixth biggest ever daily decline.
"The U.S. and Canadian markets continued their correction...on a more stable tone," Toronto-based brokerage firm RBC Dominion Securities said in a report.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average posted a bigger loss, dropping 98 points to close at 6303.7.
With equity markets jittery, portfolio managers took the opportunity to lock in profits from strong market gains earlier this year, analysts said.
Energy, consumer products, conglomerates and financial services led 11 of 14 sub-groups lower. There were modest gains in communications, gold and real estate.

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd was the top active today, falling 0.85 to 19.80 in heavy turnover of 8.6 million shares. Bre-X said joint venture talks with Barrick Gold Corp were proceeding slowly over the rich Busang gold find. Barrick added one to 39.50 on 2.0 million shares.
* Bank stocks were hammered for a second straight day. Royal Bank of Canada fell 1.35 to 46.40, while Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce surrendered 1.05 to 53.70.
* TrizecHahn Corp rose 0.20 to 28.65 after the real estate firm acquired two U.S. office properties for US$80 million.
